facts.label: Segundo condicional
facts.sub: Use If + passado simples para uma situação imaginária e would + verbo para o resultado: If I had a car, I would travel. Não use would depois de If.

facts.label: If + passado
facts.sub: Para situações imaginárias, use If + passado simples: If I had a car. Isso fala do presente, mesmo com o verbo no passado. Depois, na outra parte, use would + verbo.

facts.label: Resultado
facts.sub: O resultado imaginário usa would + verbo base: I would save time, we would travel. A contração é I’d, you’d, we’d. Na escrita simples, prefira would.

pages.title: Mito ou fato? · 1/2

items.s: We use If I had… for situations that are not real now.

items.why: After If, we use the past: If I had.

items.s: “I would go” talks about an imaginary result.

pages.instruction: Decida e explique com suas palavras.

solo: Aluno responde e justifica; você mostra a pista.
group: Cada aluno decide sozinho, depois compare as respostas e peça uma justificativa.
Corrija pela pista do texto, não só dizendo “certo/errado”.
extra90: Peça que cada aluno invente uma pergunta igual para o colega.
answers: We use If I had… for situations that are not real now. → Verdadeiro (Yes.)
After If, we use would. → Falso (After If, we use the past: If I had.)
“I would go” talks about an imaginary result. → Verdadeiro (Yes.)

pages.title: A parking lot · 1/3
paragraphs: It is a sunny Friday afternoon in Denver. Ana is leaving a big parking lot on foot. Cars drive past her, one after another. Her friend Finn waits at the corner with a map. He has an old car, but she doesn’t. They start to dream about a trip.
“Ana, you walk to work every day. Do you want a car?” says Finn. “Of course! If I had a car, I would save time every day.” says Ana. “If you had one, where would you park it?” says Finn.
